Friday Night Football at GIO Stadium has far more riding on it than the respective ladder positions suggest, as the Raiders host Brisbane in a matchup loaded with desperation, emotion, and a little revenge. Canberra’s finals hopes remain incredibly faint, but they are still alive. Wins over Brisbane and North Queensland, combined with their Round 26 bye, could get the Raiders to 30 competition points, and leave them praying other results fall their way. Brisbane, meanwhile, have endured one of the worst premiership defences in modern NRL history and are now fighting simply to avoid an unthinkable wooden spoon.
Then there is Josh Papali’i. Friday night will be the Canberra legend’s final home appearance, with GIO Stadium even being temporarily transformed into “Papa’s House” for the occasion. Papali’i has been promoted into the starting front row, and you can guarantee the Raiders faithful will turn this into one of the most emotional home games of the season.
My numbers are not miles away from the current spread, but the circumstances push me toward Canberra. With the Broncos broken, Reece Walsh gone for the season and the Raiders needing a win, I’ll take Canberra -10.5.

Raiders Refuse to Let Season Die
Canberra looked like a team whose finals hopes were virtually finished heading into last week’s trip to Sharks Stadium, yet they produced one of their gutsiest performances of the season to upset Cronulla 24-20. Against a Sharks side sitting firmly in the top 4 conversation, the Raiders absorbed an early 8-0 deficit, fought their way to an 18-14 halftime lead and then survived a frantic final quarter to keep their season alive.
Joseph Tapine delivered the decisive moment after the Sharks had regained a 20-18 advantage, powering through five defenders to score underneath the posts in the 57th minute. From there, Canberra defended their lead despite Cronulla receiving several opportunities to steal the game late.
It was exactly the type of performance Ricky Stuart would have wanted after the Raiders’ form had again become inconsistent. Canberra have enough attacking talent through Kaeo Weekes, Ethan Strange, Ethan Sanders, Matthew Timoko and Xavier Savage, but their success still starts with the middle. Tapine, Papalii, Zac Hosking and Ata Mariota must generate the field position that allows the young spine to play with freedom.
Morgan Smithies’ failed HIA against Cronulla rules him out this week, forcing Mariota to lock, while Corey Horsburgh returns through the interchange. Simi Sasagi is also back from a shoulder problem, strengthening the centres.

NRL Casualty Ward: Mitchell eyes comeback; Surgery for Doueihi, Walsh
South Sydney star Latrell Mitchell is in the mix to return from a nerve injury that has kept him sidelined since Round 11 for Saturday's showdown with the Warriors.
The centre has missed 11 games with the injury but has been named in the extended squad for this weekend's match at Accor Stadium.
Mitchell trained on Monday and has been running more freely as he builds up to a highly-anticipated return.
The Rabbitohs have lost Adam Elliott to a groin injury, with the veteran expected to miss two to three weeks with a strained adductor.
Meanwhile, Warriors halfback Luke Metcalf will miss the remainder of the regular season after suffering a hamstring injury in last week's win over Brisbane.
"The timeline for him will be deep into the finals but you never know," coach Andrew Webster said on Thursday.
"I think this is probably the most optimistic I've seen him when he knows he's got a plan and when he knows he wants to attack something."
With Te Maire Martin at least another week away from returning from a hamstring injury, rookie Luke Hanson will step into the halves for Saturday's clash with the Rabbitohs.
"We want to make sure we get it right but Te Maire is progressing well," Webster said.
Wests Tigers halfback Adam Doueihi will undergo season-ending surgery that will rule him out of Lebanon's World Cup campaign.
The playmaker dislocated his shoulder in a Round 9 loss to the Sharks and initially delayed surgery in an attempt to kickstart the Tigers finals campaign.
The 28-year-old returned to the field in Round 17 but fresh scans have shown Doueihi requires immediate surgery, with the halfback to go under the knife later this week.
"New scans on Adam's shoulder have showed the time has come to have his reconstruction done. This gives him enough time to be ready for the start of the 2027 season," Wests Tigers head of high performance Peter Moussa said.
Meanwhile, Tigers five-eighth Latu Fainu has suffered a low-grade hamstring injury at training. Fainu was set to return this week after serving a three-game suspension, but will now be sidelined for 1-2 weeks with his latest injury.
In positive news, Sunia Turuva has been named on the six-man bench despite suffering a knee injury last week, while Alex Twal is set to return after missing Round 24 due to illness.
The Roosters will also welcome back James Tedesco from an ankle injury for Sunday's clash against the Tigers at Allianz Stadium.
The Melbourne Storm will welcome back Harry Grant from a hamstring strain for Thursday's clash with the Panthers.
The hooker suffered the injury in the Round 21 loss to the Rabbitohs and is on track to return this week alongside centre Jack Howarth (shoulder) and forward Alec MacDonald (concussion).
Less positive news for Jahrome Hughes , who remains sidelined with a hamstring injury.
Mixed news on the injury front for Penrith, with gun centre Casey McLean back on deck from a broken hand, however Paul Alamoti has been ruled out with a hamstring injury.
Broncos superstar Reece Walsh has had surgery on his ankle and is facing an eight-week recovery time.

Dolphins vs Eels Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 25 2026
August 20 th 2026, 3:43pm , By: Scooby
The second NRL game on Friday night heads to Brisbane as the Dolphins host the Eels . Always promising a high scoring game, the Dolphins will again be looking to display an impressive standard of rugby league. The Eels will not want that to occur and while playing for pride, could also disrupt the Finals plans for the hosts. This sets the stage for an intriguing contest and Before You Bet is here to look at what is ahead in this match.
Also, Before You Bet will be providing free previews and betting tips for EVERY game in the 2026 NRL season, so make sure to head over to our NRL Tips regularly to keep up to date with all of our free content.
Dolphins vs Eels Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 25 2026
Taking care of business
In a tricky road trip to face the Sea Eagles, the Dolphins did what was required in their 22-0 victory. Hardly exhibiting relentless pressure, the Dolphins will be most pleased by the fact that their defence was resolute and wasn’t cracked over 80 minutes. They strangled their opponents by missing just 26 tackles and allowing only 1 line break. This meant that they could build pressure with their attack; with 51% possession and a 74% completion rate, they averaged 9.9m per carry and made 672 PCM’s. This saw them create 6 line breaks, while continuing to play fast and resemble a team headed towards the Finals.
Spirited and determined
The Eels caused a huge upset with their 32-30 home victory over the Cowboys. Expected to struggle against a superior opponent, the Eels failed to play to the predicted script of the match. Rather, they dictated the terms of the contest and played freely in attack. They gave themselves every chance of performing well by completing at 90% with 52% possession, running for 10.5m per carry, making 642 PCM’s, and creating 7 line breaks. If this standard had consistently been produced throughout 2026, they would be preparing for the upcoming Finals series.
Stats that matter
- These two sides have only met three times, with the home team never capturing victory. Here, the Dolphins strike at 59% compared to the Eels 45%.
- The average margin of victory is high (16.7 points) in their history, with two blowout 28-point wins dragging the total up. They been high scoring games too, with an average of 54.7 points.
- The Dolphins are the superior team on both sides of the ball in 2026. They score 27ppg in attack and allow just 21ppg defensively. In contrast, the Eels manage to score just 20ppg in attack while allowing 28ppg.
A proper Top 8 team
Without taking anything away from the Eels victory last week, they will face a harder opponent this weekend. To increase the difficulty, they also must perform on the road with a short turnaround. With the benefit of 7 days to prepare and returning home, the Dolphins should be at their best to cope with what their opponents throw at them. There were positive signs that both sides of the ball were improving for them, and they will especially take confidence away from their most recent defensive effort. They’re improving their ability to ‘strangle’ teams out of a contest and raising to a higher intensity should be a focus for them ahead of this match. They are embedded into the Top 8 for a reason and this is there chance to make a statement.
Despite being resilient in recent weeks, the Eels are about to find out the difference between them and a real Top 8 team. That is not to suggest their performance will be poor; in their last 4 matches the margin of victory has been 6 points or less. Once the home side gathers momentum, they will be too hard for the visitors to stop.

'Carry on what he's built': Raiders' vow before Papa's swansong
Raiders hooker Tom Starling has declared his side has a responsibility to build on the legacy left by retiring club legend Josh Papalii.
The prop will play his final game at GIO Stadium on Friday night before hanging up the boots at the end of the season after a decorated 16-year career.
Papalii will retire as Canberra's most capped player, having arrived in the capital as a fresh-faced teenager and developed into a leader both on and off the field.
The one, the only, Josh Papali'i
"No one's going to replace Papa, but we can carry on what he's built here over the last 15 years," Starling told NRL.com. "He made his debut when I was starting high school so he's going to leave a lasting legacy here for years to come.
"He's still going to be around the club in some shape or form so it's going to be good to have him here and he's set up a wonderful platform for the future for us to continue on with. He's a massive part of this club and will continue to be a massive part of it."

The prop made 24 appearances for Queensland throughout his career, winning seven State of Origin series. He also represented Australia on 11 occasions and played in the Kangaroos 2013 World Cup triumph.
Papalii pledged his allegiance to Samoa later in his career and has played a key role in the Pacific nation's development into an international power.
Through it all, the Raiders were central to Papalii's career, the prop to notch his 341st NRL appearance for the club on Friday night.
Papalii stands tall in the moment of need again
Arguably his most famous moment in the lime green was immortalised on Monday when a mural of his match-winning try in the 2019 preliminary final was unveiled at GIO Stadium.
While his legacy on the field is plain to see, Starling said Papalii drove the off-field culture that has allowed the Raiders to enjoy success throughout the past decade.
"You look at him and see a big, dominant figure, but you get down to Canberra and realise he's a big cuddly bear," Starling said. "He's the first locker as you walk into the changeroom and he's always there early.
"My favourite part of the morning is going in and giving him a big hug. When I first moved to Canberra, he was as welcoming as ever. You ask anyone who's come into contact with Papa and they all say he makes you feel welcome.
"He'll give you the shirt off his back anytime you ask, he makes everyone feel welcome and he's what a Canberra Raider should be."
The Raiders don't need any additional motivation on Friday night, but they have found it in multiple places.
Last Saturday's victory over the Sharks kept their slim finals hopes alive. With the bye next weekend, Canberra need to beat Brisbane and hope North Queensland lose to the Tigers next week to set up a winner-takes-all Round 27 showdown in Townsville.
